newsitem.title: UK: LME copper unchanged in late London.
newsitem.headline: LME copper unchanged in late London.

text.p: London Metal Exchange (LME) three months copper was scarcely changed from the kerb in subdued late inter-office activity on Wednesday.
The day had earlier been marked by failure to challenge overhead resistance at $1,950 and a narrowing in the newly-established contango, traders said.
Final kerb business was at $1,922 a tonne, down from a $1,944 peak and just $2 up from Tuesday. By 1800 GMT when Comex ended LME copper was bid at $1,920 after a desultory foray towards $1,930.
Brokerage Rudolf Wolff said in its Evening Metal Report that further declines in LME stocks were likely to help copper.
But the kerb close had been disappointing and "any rally is likely to find difficulty in overcoming stiff resistance between 1950-70".
Aluminium failed to make progress above $1,400 and was bid at around that level in late London.
